response:
That's a painful contradiction to sit with—now that he's suddenly available and affectionate, you're being asked to give warmth you didn't receive when you needed it most. It makes sense that you'd feel resentful, or even numb, rather than instantly ready to reconnect. Five years of emotional starvation doesn't disappear because he's finally noticing you.

Your feelings are valid, and so is your exhaustion. You're carrying a full-time job and two kids alone while he's rediscovering a social life. It's fair to want acknowledgment of that imbalance before you can open up again. You might tell him honestly that you can't just flip a switch, and that you need him to understand the years you spent feeling unseen. If you can, consider couples counseling to help both of you talk through this gap. You deserve a partnership where your needs matter too—not just when it's convenient for him.
